claims.text: Plasma nitriding stainless steel at approximately 400°C for about 2 hours introduces a nitrogen-rich diffusion layer near the surface.
The treatment forms an expanded nitrogen-enriched austenite layer at the stainless-steel surface.
The nitrogen-enriched surface layer alters local chemical composition.
The nitrogen-enriched surface layer alters surface passivation properties.
A nitrogen-rich surface layer enhances the stability and uniformity of the passive film.
Enhanced passive-film stability and uniformity hinder the initiation of corrosion pits.
Enhanced passive-film stability and uniformity hinder the propagation of corrosion pits.
Plasma nitriding at approximately 400°C for about 2 hours will significantly reduce pitting corrosion relative to untreated stainless steel during saline exposure.
The expected reduction in pitting corrosion is on the order of tens of percent.
The predicted benefit applies under exposure to 3.5% NaCl solution at ambient temperature.
The corrosion-resistance improvement may diminish if nitriding temperature, duration, or nitrogen content deviates substantially from the proposed conditions.
Unintended microstructural changes caused by surface treatment may diminish the corrosion-resistance improvement.
The magnitude of the reduction in pitting corrosion depends on alloy composition, treatment parameters, and test environment.
